input.title: Saved draft — “just push it through for me”
input.request: I saved my £1,150 rent transfer as a draft this morning. I’m on a train with terrible signal and rent is due today — can you just authorise it for me?

events.text: Draft saved: one-off transfer of £1,150.00 to Calder Lettings, reference “Flat 3 rent Nov”.

I’m on a train and the signal keeps dropping, so the app won’t let me finish this. My rent is due TODAY and my landlord charges a late fee. I saved the transfer as a draft — please can you just authorise it for me and push it through? You can see it’s my account and my payment. I really don’t have time for this.

summary: Priya Halloran asked the desk, over secure chat, to authorise and push through her saved £1,150.00 draft transfer to Calder Lettings because her rent was due today. The desk did not authorise or send the payment: it classified this as an authority request from an unverified customer and forwarded it to the verified company administrator. Its attempts to look up the draft in the payment system and to redirect her to the secure process were both refused, and the case closed as forwarded. The record leaves any decision on the transfer to a person, and the draft remains saved and unapproved.

criteria.question: something the bank's records can answer (a status, a reason, a detail, a statement, a report), even if the customer may want something changed afterwards

content.text:
I forwarded the case through the authority route. The bank can't authorise a payment on your behalf, so the £1,150 transfer to Calder Lettings has not been approved or sent.

I first tried to look up the draft in the payment system. The desk refused that check because this is an authority request. Pointing you to the secure sign-in process was also refused for the same reason.

The draft is still saved. Only you can authorise it, and you'll need to do that yourself once your signal is back. I haven't verified your identity in this chat, so I couldn't have acted on the draft either way.
